newsitem.title: UK: Healthcare to help Hong Kong stand out, Tung says.
newsitem.headline: Healthcare to help Hong Kong stand out, Tung says.

text.p: Healthcare and other quality of life issues will be a "very high priority" for Hong Kong after its handover to China, Tung Chee-hwa, soon to be the territory's chief executive, said on Monday.
In one of his last public addresses before the midnight (1600 GMT) handover, Tung told a conference on telemedicine he foresaw a "compassionate and democratic" society in Hong Kong.
He said Hong Kong's progress in health care had been overlooked by those admiring its strong economy.
"We have one of the lowest infant mortality rates, longest life expectancy and lowest incidence of smoking anywhere," Tung told audiences in London and Hong Kong via a video link.
Tung, who will be sworn in soon after the midnight handover, said technology like telemedicine -- which uses remote video and computer links -- would improve life for Hong Kong people.

"I see an increasingly affluent and well-educated population, an ever-improving physical environment that ensures a higher quality of life and a high-calibre medical care service that promotes wellness," he said.
"I see a compassionate and democratic society with a social welfare system that encourages self-reliance while caring for the sick, the weak and the elderly," he added.

Organisers of the telemedicine conference, Britain's Royal Society of Medicine, the Chinese University of Hong Kong and Beijing's Health Ministry, started their conference in a Hong Kong governed by Britain and planned to end it later on Tuesday in Hong Kong after it becomes a Special Administrative Region of China.
